title: The Singer Who Died Broke With Millions

beats.say: He earned more than movie stars in his prime, but when he died, he couldn't afford his own funeral.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a solitary silhouette walking down a rain-slick street under sodium streetlights at night.

beats.say: That was 1973, and the man was Bobby Darin. How did a legend with massive chart hits run completely out of cash?
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a massive Art Deco theater marquee, weathered and dark against a cold blue hour sky.

beats.say: Most people assume that when you make millions, your bank account just grows on its own.
beats.visual: Close up of heavy brass vault doors reflecting a lone cold fluorescent light in an empty hallway.

beats.say: That's wrong. Darin's gross revenue was huge, but his cash flow was bleeding out every single week.
beats.visual: High angle shot of a single hand dropping a heavy brass key onto a wet asphalt curb.

beats.say: Where was the money actually going before it ever hit his pocket?
beats.visual: Extreme close up of water rushing down a dark concrete storm drain under a sodium streetlamp.

beats.say: He funded his own movie studio, a record label, and a lavish lifestyle that required constant massive inflows.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a man standing at the edge of a high concrete rooftop, looking down at a distant highway.

beats.say: When his hits slowed down in the late 1960s, those fixed overhead costs didn't stop.
beats.visual: Wide shot of an empty concrete underpass cut by harsh fluorescent lights and deep shadows.

beats.say: So why couldn't he just sell his assets to stay afloat?
beats.visual: Extreme close up of a heavy iron chain resting on wet, dark stone in the rain.

beats.say: Because owning valuable things isn't the same as having spendable cash when emergencies hit.
beats.visual: Low angle shot of a towering concrete bridge pier stretching up into a foggy, overcast sky.

beats.say: He confused top-line revenue with true net wealth, and the math caught up to him.
beats.visual: Extreme wide shot of a single car driving across an empty bridge over dark, open water at night.

beats.say: Keep your overhead low and your cash liquid. Follow for the money rules school never taught you.
beats.visual: Silhouette of a person walking away down a dark, fog-cut alley lit by a single practical bulb.

caption:
Gross revenue doesn't equal net wealth. Keep your cash liquid.
